title: Lightweight shim & resumable parsed-stream SDK samples (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a compact, idiomatic set of SDK examples and a tiny shim pattern that demonstrates: (1) progressive streaming with resumable session tokens, (2) function/tool calling handshake and replay-safe confirmations, and (3) structured-output parsing + schema validation across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Deliverables: sample code in repo, migration playbook for customers, and a small compatibility shim library that makes older client code interoperable with our new framed streaming protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Three language samples (TS/Py/Go) added under sdk/samples/streaming-tools with README and tests
Examples show resumable sessions: client can resume a stream using session_token and offset without double-executing side effects
Tool/function calling handshake includes explicit call-id and replay-confirmation pattern (call-id ack + idempotency-key) in examples
Structured output examples include JSON Schema and runtime validation snippet in each language
Migration playbook (docs/migration/shim-guide.md) with recommended integration steps and known limitations
Performance smoke test: end-to-end streaming latency within 10% of current non-resumable flow under representative load
technical_notes: Design decision: prefer a minimal transport shim that maps the new framed stream events to existing incremental APIs; avoid adding new surface area to public SDKs — expose a tiny adapter in each language that can be opt-in.

Resumable session model: server issues session_token on initial handshake; every emitted chunk includes sequence_offset; client stores last_ack_offset locally and can request resume(session_token, next_offset). Server must support idempotent tool-call replay when call_id <= last_seen_call_id.

Python pattern (example):
async def stream_session(url: str, token: str):
    async for frame in shim.connect(url, token):
        # frame = {"offset": int, "payload": bytes, "type": "output" | "tool_call"}
        yield parse_payload(frame)
# tool calls include call_id metadata and transient lock to ensure at-most-once semantics

Structured output: provide canonical JSON Schema for a typical tool response and an envelope schema. Runtime validators shipped in TS (ajv), Py (jsonschema), Go (github.com/xeipuuv/gojsonschema) with small glue code in examples.

Backward compatibility: adapter will transform legacy line-delimited incremental events into framed events; migration playbook recommends opt-in flag `useFramedStreaming: true` so customers can toggle while rolling out server-side support.

Security: shim does not change auth; session_token is bearer-scoped and short-lived. Replay window limited to last 1 hour; audit logs must link call_id to final side-effect commit (see release notes).
examples:
Python minimal sample (pseudo):
async with shim.connect(endpoint, token) as s:
    async for frame in s.stream():
        if frame['type'] == 'tool_call':
            ack = await s.call_tool(frame['tool_name'], frame['payload'], call_id=frame['call_id'])
        else:
            validate(frame['payload'], SCHEMA)
# resumption:
await s.resume(next_offset=last_offset + 1)

Corner cases: large binary attachments in tool payloads should be referenced by content-id and fetched via signed URL; resumable offsets operate at logical chunk boundaries (server negotiates chunk_size per session).
